name: DeepFluoro
aka: DeepFluoroLabeling-IPCAI2020; JHU cadaveric PAO CT + fluoroscopy; xvr-data/deepfluoro; diffdrrdata DeepFluoro
anatomy: pelvis, proximal femora, lower lumbar vertebrae and upper sacrum (6 cadaveric lower torsos)
size: 6 specimens; HDF5 release 3.43 GB with 366 pose-registered frames (Siemens Cios Fusion); vendor record doi:10.7281/T1/C304HZ is 38.3 GB with pre/post-op CTs, all fluoroscopy, FTRAC fiducial and sawbones data
annotation_detail: per-frame extrinsic pose and calibrated intrinsics; 2-D and 3-D segmentations with six labels (left/right hemipelvis, vertebrae, upper sacrum, left/right femur); 14 bilateral pelvic landmarks
how_to_get: JHU Research Data Repository (Dataverse) DOI 10.7281/T1/IFSXNV (HDF5, full and 2x-16x downsampled) and 10.7281/T1/C304HZ (vendor DICOM); also re-hosted in huggingface.co/datasets/eigenvivek/xvr-data; the JHU site sits behind Cloudflare, so scripted downloads may need a browser-like client
paper: Grupp RB et al. Automatic annotation of hip anatomy in fluoroscopy for robust and efficient 2D/3D registration. IJCARS 2020;15:759-769. doi:10.1007/s11548-020-02162-7
notes: The calibration anchor for CT-to-C-arm parity, but the HDF5 frames are log-transformed and cropped display images and the vertebrae are one lumped label, so only the vendor DICOMs speak to the device's native intensity.

name: Ljubljana 2D-3D-GS (lumbar spine gold standard)
aka: Tomazevic gold standard; 2D-3D-GS.zip
size: 1 specimen; CT, MR and 18 X-ray images with gold-standard registrations; 75.4 MB zip plus a 0.7 MB user guide
annotation_detail: gold-standard rigid registrations between each X-ray and CT/MR, with evaluation software; CT supplied as per-vertebra crops L1-L5
how_to_get: The lab page links 2D-3D-GS.zip directly, but the user guide states the data may only be obtained and used after signing an agreement form with the Laboratory of Imaging Technologies, University of Ljubljana
license: CC BY-NC-ND (per the lab page), plus the agreement form named in the user guide
paper: Tomazevic D, Likar B, Pernus F. 'Gold Standard' 2D/3D registration of X-ray to CT and MR images. MICCAI 2002, LNCS 2489. doi:10.1007/3-540-45787-9_58
notes: The only public spine set with true per-level CT and a known X-ray pose, but it is one bare specimen on a turntable with a flat-panel detector, not a C-arm and not a torso with soft tissue.

name: Ljubljana 3D-2D-GS-CA (cerebral angiography gold standard)
aka: the 'Ljubljana' set in DiffDRR, DiffPose and xvr; xvr-data/ljubljana
anatomy: cerebral vasculature and skull (10 endovascular patients)
size: 10 patients; one 3D-DSA (rotational C-arm) volume and four 2-D images (AP and LAT DSA, AP and LAT MAX) each; ten zips of 85-120 MB plus a gold-standard zip
annotation_detail: per 2-D image a 4x4 detector-to-world matrix and X-ray source position from fiducial alignment (mean TRE 0.033-0.077 mm); vessel centreline target points; 400 initial displacements per case
how_to_get: Ten zips are linked from the lab page; the user guide states use requires a signed agreement form with the laboratory; also re-hosted in huggingface.co/datasets/eigenvivek/xvr-data with the authors' permission
license: CC BY-NC-ND (per the lab page), plus the agreement form named in the user guide
paper: Mitrovic U, Spiclin Z, Likar B, Pernus F. 3D-2D registration of cerebral angiograms: a method and evaluation on clinical images. IEEE TMI 2013;32(8):1550-1563. doi:10.1109/TMI.2013.2259844
notes: Living patients with exact C-arm geometry, but the 3-D image is a C-arm 3D-DSA rather than CT, the 2-D images are float exports normalised to 0-1, and there is no spine; Greg's manifest holds only the lumbar Tomazevic set, not this one.

name: Femur multi-view X-ray/CT dataset (Flepp et al.)
aka: dataset_ipcai.zip; xvr-data/femur; MultiviewXrayCT-Registration
size: 5 CTs (Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha) and real calibrated X-rays from 10 views per specimen at about 9 degree steps (about 50 images, Siemens Fluorospot Compact S1, 976x976); one 6.7 GB zip
annotation_detail: C-arm pose per image from a 3D-printed radiolucent marker with 16 metal spheres clamped to a K-wire in the femur; bone contours segmented on control views for mRPD evaluation
how_to_get: Download dataset_ipcai.zip from Zenodo record 15753063 under its research-only licence; also re-hosted in huggingface.co/datasets/eigenvivek/xvr-data; the registration code is licensed on request (patent EP25168706.7 pending)
license: Research-Only Dataset License (non-commercial academic research; commercial use prohibited)
paper: Flepp R et al. Automatic multi-view X-ray/CT registration using bone substructure contours. IJCARS 2025;20:1401-1408. doi:10.1007/s11548-025-03391-4 (arXiv:2506.13292)
notes: A second real C-arm model (Fluorospot Compact S1) with fiducial-grade pose and paired CT, downloadable now, but the anatomy is distal femur, so it serves device calibration rather than vertebral appearance.

name: Geneva hip 2D-3D registration gold standard
aka: D'Isidoro/Schmid hip phantom set; Yareta 2kw5s2jadbbv3ngtkzsovihtnu
size: 1 phantom CT (Philips Brilliance 64) and 19 fluoroscopy frames (Philips BV Pulsera image intensifier, 1000x1000, 12-bit); 481 files, 394 MB
annotation_detail: gold-standard pose per frame from uncertainty-modelled fiducial calibration, with motion-capture pose for comparison; calibrated projection matrices
how_to_get: Public archive on Yareta (University of Geneva), DOI 10.26037/yareta:2kw5s2jadbbv3ngtkzsovihtnu; the record also lists a contract on the use of data
paper: D'Isidoro F, Chenes C, Ferguson SJ, Schmid J. A new 2D-3D registration gold-standard dataset for the hip joint based on uncertainty modeling. Med Phys 2021;48(10):5991-6006. doi:10.1002/mp.15124
notes: An image-intensifier C-arm with exact geometry, useful for the device term, but the phantom has no realistic soft tissue and no spine.

name: SpineSAC
aka: IGRS-Imaging SpineSAC phantom C-arm 2D/3D registration set (HTIC, IIT Madras)
anatomy: lumbar spine sawbone phantoms (one closed, two open)
size: 3 phantoms, 3 CT series, 59 AP + lateral acquisition scenarios from several C-arms (40 train / 10 validation / 9 test); about 4.1 GB
annotation_detail: per scenario two 3x4 projection matrices (AP+LP), 6-DoF ground-truth pose and an initial pose, vertebra ROI boxes per view
how_to_get: Google Drive folder linked from the GitHub README; download each subfolder under its original name
license: not stated for the data (code licence shown as Apache-2.0, README badge says MIT)
paper: none found; cite the repository
notes: The widest spread of C-arm vendors with known projection matrices on spine anatomy, but sawbones carry no soft tissue and no paper documents the ground-truth method.

name: C-ArmLSpine
aka: PRSCS-Net data; Zenodo 22768651
anatomy: lumbar spine and sacrum (thoracic reach about T11-T12)
size: 149 cases: AP and lateral spot frames plus one CBCT from the same FIRST Surgio-B51 mobile C-arm; 15.6 GB zip
annotation_detail: release carries no labels or poses; Greg's own pipeline registered 296 frames and projected per-level boxes T11-sacrum
how_to_get: Direct download of C-ArmLSpine.zip from Zenodo
paper: Zhang et al. PRSCS-Net: progressive 3D/2D rigid registration network with the guidance of single-view cycle synthesis. Medical Image Analysis 2024;97:103283. doi:10.1016/j.media.2024.103283
notes: The closest public match to the intraoperative lumbar C-arm problem because X-ray and CBCT come from one device on one table, but pose must be recovered by registration and one case still carries identifying DICOM headers.

name: Balgrist ex-vivo lumbar CT + C-arm set (Jecklin et al.)
aka: X23D domain-adaptation dataset; IXGS ex-vivo data
anatomy: lumbar spine in fresh-frozen whole human torsos
size: 13 torsos (10 train, 3 test) plus 6 validation specimens; 1,017 real fluoroscopy shots paired with same-pose DRRs, giving 4,337 localized vertebra images
annotation_detail: camera pose per X-ray from 14 implanted steel fiducials located in a post-fiducial CT; vertebra segmentations by trained specialists (Mimics); Siemens Cios Spin main set, Ziehm Vision and Vision FD on validation specimens
how_to_get: Not released; the Sci Rep 2025 IXGS paper states the ex-vivo paired dataset (real X-rays, DRRs, calibration) is available from the corresponding author on reasonable request and that a small test subset will appear at github.com/MrMonk3y/IXGS (empty as of 2026-10-17)
paper: Jecklin S et al. Domain adaptation strategies for 3D reconstruction of the lumbar spine using real fluoroscopy data. Medical Image Analysis 2024;98:103322. doi:10.1016/j.media.2024.103322
notes: The best fit in existence for CT-to-C-arm parity at the lumbar spine (soft-tissue torsos, three C-arm models, fiducial pose), held back by a pending patent; sources.yaml has an unsent request draft (balgrist_exvivo_request).

name: Utrecht 2D-3D registration gold standard (van de Kraats et al.)
aka: ISI Utrecht spine 3DRX/CT/MR/X-ray database
size: spine images in 3DRX, CT and MR with 2-D X-rays; specimen and image counts not verified
annotation_detail: gold-standard transformations from the calibrated geometry of a Philips 3D rotational X-ray system combined with 3-D/3-D registration
how_to_get: The paper points to http://www.isi.uu.nl/Research/Databases/, which no longer accepts connections and has no Wayback snapshot; only the authors could supply a copy
paper: van de Kraats EB, Penney GP, Tomazevic D, van Walsum T, Niessen WJ. Standardized evaluation methodology for 2-D-3-D registration. IEEE TMI 2005;24(9):1177-1189. doi:10.1109/TMI.2005.853240
notes: Historically public spine 2D/3D benchmark whose host is gone, so it is recorded to stop re-searching rather than as a source.

name: Vienna porcine head 2D/3D gold standard (Pawiro et al.)
aka: Validation for 2D/3D registration I; MedUni Vienna pig head
anatomy: fresh porcine cadaver head with fiducials
size: 1 specimen; 64-slice CT, 3 T MR (T1, T2, PD), Elekta Synergy CBCT, kV AP and lateral and MV AP and lateral projections
annotation_detail: world-to-camera matrices for the AP and lateral views from fiducial markers; source-isocentre 1000 mm, isocentre-detector 536 mm (kV)
how_to_get: The paper states the data set and gold standard are available from the corresponding author (W. Birkfellner, Medical University of Vienna)
paper: Pawiro SA et al. Validation for 2D/3D registration I: a new gold standard data set. Med Phys 2011;38(3):1481-1490. doi:10.1118/1.3553402
notes: A soft-tissue specimen with exact kV geometry on a radiotherapy imager, but the anatomy is a pig head, so it informs device and soft-tissue terms only.

name: Pig lower-limb IOERT 2D-3D registration data (Goswami et al.)
aka: Pig data for 2D-3D intensity-based registration
anatomy: porcine lower limb phantom with an electron-radiotherapy applicator
size: 1 specimen; preoperative CT, CBCT with and without soft tissue, 7 C-arm projections with and without soft tissue
annotation_detail: C-arm geometric calibration from fiducials on the applicator; a matrices file (MatricesSoftTissue) is included but its contents are not described on the page
how_to_get: IEEE DataPort, DOI 10.21227/gxpd-d998; listed as open access but files need a free IEEE account login
paper: Goswami SS et al. A new workflow for image-guided intraoperative electron radiotherapy using projection-based pose tracking. IEEE Access 2020. doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2020.3011915
notes: Small paired C-arm/CT set with soft tissue on and off, useful only for a soft-tissue ablation check since there is no spine.

name: Thorax X-ray and CT interventional dataset (Xia et al.)
aka: pig lung nonrigid 2D/3D registration dataset; Zenodo 1400558 (concept 997887)
anatomy: ex-vivo porcine lung model at several inflation states
size: 3.3 GB of CT volumes, CT scouts and X-rays (DICOM) plus 18 kB of landmarks
annotation_detail: 120 landmarks per 3-D volume; 8 bronchial-tree landmarks on each 2-D CT scout and X-ray
how_to_get: Direct download from Zenodo (Images.rar, Landmarks.rar, Documentation.pdf)
paper: Xia W, Jin Q, Ni C, Wang Y, Gao X. Thorax x-ray and CT interventional dataset for nonrigid 2D/3D image registration evaluation. Med Phys 2018;45(11):5343-5351. doi:10.1002/mp.13174
notes: Lung-only nonrigid benchmark with no bone or spine and no stated projection matrices, so its value for vertebral parity is minimal.

name: UCLA kV/MV setup radiographs with planning CT (Charters et al.)
aka: vertebral body misalignment detection dataset
size: 527 patients: 2,486 orthogonal kV image pairs (254 patients), 58 unpaired AP kV images, 250 patients with AP MV images; planning CTs with DICOM REG
annotation_detail: DICOM REG transforms aligning planning-CT DRRs to each treatment radiograph
how_to_get: Data availability statement: not public because of sensitive personal information; available upon reasonable request from the authors
paper: Charters JA et al. Automated detection of vertebral body misalignments in orthogonal kV and MV guided radiotherapy: application to a comprehensive retrospective dataset. Biomed Phys Eng Express 2024;10(2):025039. doi:10.1088/2057-1976/ad2baa
notes: Hundreds of living patients with real kV spine radiographs registered to CT, the largest such pairing known, but release depends on a request the authors framed as restricted.

name: LIDC-IDRI (CT plus chest radiographs)
aka: TCIA LIDC-IDRI; IDC lidc_idri
size: 1,010 patients with CT; 290 of them also have a chest radiograph (237 DX + 53 CR series, about 4.6 GB) per an IDC v25 query
annotation_detail: CT lung-nodule outlines and ratings from four readers; radiograph annotations not checked
how_to_get: TCIA manifest with the NBIA Data Retriever, or IDC (idc-index / s5cmd) filtered to Modality CR/DX for the 290 patients
paper: Armato SG III et al. The LIDC and IDRI: a completed reference database of lung nodules on CT scans. Med Phys 2011;38(2):915-931. doi:10.1118/1.3528204; data doi:10.7937/K9/TCIA.2015.LO9QL9SX
notes: 290 living patients with CT and a same-patient radiograph, but chest-only, no pose, and an unknown interval between the two studies; listed as planned (tier 2) in sources.yaml, not fetched.

name: COVID-19-NY-SBU (CT plus CR/DX)
aka: Stony Brook University COVID-19 Positive Cases; IDC covid_19_ny_sbu
size: 1,384 patients; 439 have both CT and CR/DX per IDC v25 (CR 11,509 series 172 GB, DX 2,623 series 39 GB, CT 3,730 series 286 GB); radiographs mostly chest, 365 CR abdomen series
annotation_detail: patient-level clinical CSV only; no image annotations
how_to_get: TCIA manifest with the NBIA Data Retriever or IDC; select CR/DX series for the 439 patients that also have CT
paper: Saltz J et al. Stony Brook University COVID-19 Positive Cases [data set]. TCIA 2021. doi:10.7937/TCIA.BBAG-2923
notes: The largest open same-patient CT + radiograph collection in IDC, but Greg's copy is a CT subset (443 series) with no CR/DX, so the paired half still has to be fetched.

name: COVID-19-AR (CT plus CR/DX)
aka: Chest imaging of a rural COVID-19 positive population (Arkansas); IDC covid_19_ar
size: 105 patients; 22 have both CT and CR/DX per IDC v25; 236 DX + 26 CR series (3.2 GB), 199 CT series (16 GB)
annotation_detail: clinical and genomic data files; no image annotations
how_to_get: TCIA manifest with the NBIA Data Retriever or IDC
paper: Desai S et al. Chest imaging representing a COVID-19 positive rural U.S. population. Sci Data 2020;7:414. doi:10.1038/s41597-020-00741-6; data doi:10.7937/tcia.2020.py71-5978
notes: Small add-on to NY-SBU; Greg holds 23 CT series and none of the radiographs.

name: CMB-MML (CT plus skeletal-survey radiographs)
aka: Cancer Moonshot Biobank Multiple Myeloma; IDC cmb_mml
anatomy: whole skeleton radiographs (C/T/L spine, sacrum, coccyx, pelvis, skull, extremities) and chest/abdominal CT
size: 177 subjects; IDC v25 open release: 147 patients, 87 with CT, 11 with CR/DX, 5 with both; 3 of those have abdominal CT plus lumbar or sacral spine radiographs
annotation_detail: no image annotations; days-from-registration in DICOM tag (0012,0052) allows timing between CT and radiograph
how_to_get: TCIA Data Retriever or IDC for the open radiology; head images are restricted under the NIH controlled-access policy
license: CC BY 4.0 (open radiology); restricted head images under NIH controlled access
paper: Cancer Moonshot Biobank. Multiple Myeloma Collection (CMB-MML), version 11 [data set]. TCIA. doi:10.7937/SZKB-SW39
notes: The only open TCIA collection where real lumbar and sacral radiographs sit beside the same patient's abdominal CT, but only 3 such patients; Greg's copy holds 16 CT series and no CR.

name: MIDRC Open Data Commons
aka: Medical Imaging and Data Resource Center; data.midrc.org (Gen3)
anatomy: mostly chest; also abdomen, spine, pelvis, extremities
size: 207,129 imaging studies in 89,599 cases (DX 94,587, CR 79,646, CT 25,795 studies); 10,100 cases hold both CT and CR/DX (anonymous Gen3 guppy query, 2026-10-17); among those cases' studies, spine-labelled body parts number about 300 (SPINE 93, LSPINE 50, LUMBAR_SPINE 45, CERVICAL_SPINE 39, CSPINE 34, TSPINE 22, THORACIC_SPINE 8)
annotation_detail: COVID-19 status and some study-level annotations (e.g. mRALE scores); no geometry
how_to_get: Register at data.midrc.org, accept the non-commercial or commercial Data Use Agreement during registration, build a cohort (filter cases with both CT and CR/DX) and download with the Gen3 client
license: MIDRC Data Use Agreement (non-commercial or commercial version); case-level licence field shows CC BY 4.0 on 2,150 and CC BY-NC 4.0 on 588 cases, none on the rest
paper: no single dataset paper; acknowledge MIDRC as its DUA requires
notes: The largest pool of living patients with same-patient CT and radiographs, including a few hundred spine radiograph studies, but no pose and mixed time intervals; Greg holds only the RICORD-1a CT subset distributed through TCIA.

name: BIMCV-COVID19+
aka: BIMCV COVID-19+ (Valencia regional imaging bank), iterations 1-2 and extensions
size: iteration 1: 1,311 patients with 1,380 CX, 885 DX and 163 CT studies; the IEEE DataPort record lists 7,377 CR, 9,463 DX and 6,687 CT studies (389 GB)
annotation_detail: radiology reports and anatomical/pathology labels in MIDS format; per-patient modality overlap not stated
how_to_get: IEEE DataPort (free IEEE account; page also mentions a subscription), or the BIMCV project page bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/bimcv-covid19
license: not stated on the IEEE DataPort page
paper: de la Iglesia Vaya M et al. BIMCV COVID-19+: a large annotated dataset of RX and CT images from COVID-19 patients. arXiv:2006.01174; data doi:10.21227/w3aw-rv39
notes: Images ship as PNG inside MIDS archives with an unstated bit depth and the CT-radiograph patient overlap is undocumented, so it ranks below the DICOM collections.

name: SyntheX data
aka: Synthetic data accelerates learning-based X-ray image analysis (JHU)
size: 8.7 GB: hip_imaging.zip 2.07 GB, surgical_tool_detection.zip 5.02 GB, covid.zip 1.60 GB; hip arm simulated about 20,000 images from 20 CTs
annotation_detail: task labels for hip landmark detection and segmentation, tool detection and COVID lesion segmentation; real hip test data come from DeepFluoro
how_to_get: JHU Research Data Repository DOI 10.7281/T1/2PGJQU; usage in github.com/arcadelab/SyntheX; source CTs from NMDID
paper: Gao C, Killeen BD et al. Synthetic data accelerates the development of generalizable learning-based algorithms for X-ray image analysis. Nat Mach Intell 2023. doi:10.1038/s42256-023-00629-1
notes: The published evidence that DeepDRR-style simulation can match real-data training on hip fluoroscopy; its hip images are a ready DRR-to-DeepFluoro comparison but contain no lumbar level labels.

name: Pelphix simulated and cadaver sequences
aka: Perphix datasets; pelphix_000338, pelphix_000339, liverpool
size: 279,709 training + 8,515 validation simulated frames (two 3.2 GB archives) and 256 cadaver frames (1.2 GB)
annotation_detail: surgical phase at four levels (corridor, activity, view, frame value) plus corridor, tool and anatomy supervision
how_to_get: JHU SharePoint links in the GitHub README; cite NMDID when using the simulated data
license: not stated for the data (repository shows MIT and Apache 2.0)
paper: Killeen BD et al. Pelphix: surgical phase recognition from X-ray images in percutaneous pelvic fixation. MICCAI 2023, LNCS 14228:133-143. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-43996-4_13
notes: Large simulated C-arm sequences of the pelvis with a small real cadaver test set, useful for view-distribution priors more than for vertebral appearance.

name: FluoroSeg
aka: FluoroSAM training data
size: about 3M synthetic X-rays from 1,621 CTs; 2.65 TB on Hugging Face
annotation_detail: mask and text pairs for 128 organ classes and 464 tool types
how_to_get: Accept the gating conditions (share contact information) on the Hugging Face dataset page
paper: Killeen BD et al. FluoroSAM: a language-aligned foundation model for X-ray image segmentation. MICCAI 2025. arXiv:2403.08059
notes: The largest released CT-derived X-ray segmentation set; whether its 128 classes include individual vertebra levels was not confirmed and the 2.65 TB size makes a targeted subset necessary.

name: X2CT-GAN LIDC synthetic biplanar X-rays
aka: LIDC-HDF5-256
size: LIDC-IDRI CTs (1,018 scans in the paper) with synthetic PA and lateral X-rays; about 70 GB per the README
annotation_detail: paired synthetic orthogonal views and resampled CT in HDF5; CycleGAN style transfer toward real radiographs
how_to_get: Weiyun or Dropbox links in the GitHub README
license: code GPLv3 (sidebar says LGPL-3.0); data licence not stated (source LIDC is CC BY 3.0)
paper: Ying X et al. X2CT-GAN: reconstructing CT from biplanar X-rays with generative adversarial networks. CVPR 2019. doi:10.1109/CVPR.2019.01087 (arXiv:1905.06902)
notes: A standard chest DRR benchmark whose source CTs also have 290 real radiographs in LIDC, which allows a DRR-versus-real comparison on the same patients.

name: DRR-RATE
aka: Shadow and Light DRRs of CT-RATE
size: AP and lateral DRRs for 50,188 reconstructions of the 25,692 CT-RATE volumes (21,304 patients); 7.97 GB; files are 512x512 8-bit grayscale PNG (checked on one file)
annotation_detail: inherits CT-RATE reports and 18 binary pathology labels
how_to_get: Hugging Face dataset farrell236/DRR-RATE; source CTs in CT-RATE
paper: DRR-RATE, arXiv:2406.03688; CT-RATE, arXiv:2403.17834
notes: Large but 8-bit, fixed-geometry Siddon-Jacobs DRRs thresholded at -100 HU, so it says little about C-arm image formation.

name: MedNeRF DRR set
aka: MedNeRF chest_xrays and knee_xrays
size: 20 chest and 5 knee CT instances, 72 DRRs each at 5 degree steps over 360 degrees, 128x128 PNG
annotation_detail: multi-view DRR stacks for novel-view synthesis; camera matrices built from Plastimatch geometry
how_to_get: Google Drive link in the GitHub README
license: not stated for the data (repository MIT)
paper: Corona-Figueroa A et al. MedNeRF: medical neural radiance fields for reconstructing 3D-aware CT-projections from a single X-ray. EMBC 2022. doi:10.1109/EMBC48229.2022.9871757
notes: Tiny, low-resolution knee and chest DRRs; listed for completeness of the knee search, not as a parity resource.

name: COBRA2026
aka: COBRA challenge pelvic CBCT projection dataset
anatomy: pelvis (radiotherapy patients; iliac wings, sacrum, lower lumbar in field)
size: 867 cases from six European centres (692 training public, about 750 GB; 52 validation and 123 test embargoed)
annotation_detail: per case measured projections (uint16), RTK geometry.xml, planning CT deformably registered to the CBCT, and simulated projections from the aligned CT
how_to_get: Training set from the CREATIS Lyon tomoradio warehouse without registration, using the resumable script in the COBRA2026 preprocessing GitHub repository; Zenodo holds overview PNGs and the paper
paper: Thummerer A et al. COBRA2026: a large-scale multicenter pelvic cone-beam CT projection dataset. arXiv:2607.20037
notes: The only large living-patient set with linear detector signal, exact geometry and a matched CT plus vendor-simulated projections, though from linac-mounted kV imagers rather than mobile C-arms.

name: SPARE challenge 4D-CBCT projections
aka: Sparse-view Reconstruction Challenge for Four-dimensional Cone-beam CT
anatomy: thorax (lung cancer and one liver patient; thoracic spine in field)
size: clinical Varian (5 patients, 30 scans, 2,400-3,600 projections at 1024x768) and Elekta (5 patients, 20 scans, 1,000 projections at 512x512) sets, each with a prior 4D-CT, plus Monte-Carlo simulated scans from 4D-Lung
annotation_detail: per-projection geometry relative to the CBCT frame; prior 4D-CT and PTV mask; no registration from CBCT to the prior CT
how_to_get: SPARE_PublicArchive.zip and a readme from the University of Sydney eScholarship repository (handle 2123/34378); headerless float32 projections
paper: Shieh CC et al. SPARE: sparse-view reconstruction challenge for 4D cone-beam CT from a 1-min scan. Med Phys 2019;46(9):3799-3811. doi:10.1002/mp.13687
notes: Real Varian and Elekta kV projections of living thoraces with geometry, a second linac-imager reference for COBRA, but the prior CT must be registered by the user.

name: LDCT-and-Projection-data (Mayo)
aka: Low Dose CT Image and Projection Data; AAPM/Mayo low-dose CT projections
size: 299 patients (199 open: chest and abdomen, plus a phantom; 99 head restricted); full-dose and simulated low-dose projections
annotation_detail: DICOM-CT-PD projection data with acquisition geometry; clinical reports
how_to_get: TCIA Data Retriever for the open chest, abdomen and phantom data; head data via NIH controlled access
license: CC BY 4.0 (open subset); head data under NIH controlled access
paper: Moen TR et al. Low-dose CT image and projection dataset. Med Phys 2021;48(2):902-911. doi:10.1002/mp.14594; data doi:10.7937/9NPB-2637
notes: Helical multidetector CT projections rather than cone-beam C-arm frames, useful for physics of attenuation and noise but not for C-arm geometry; listed as planned in sources.yaml, not fetched.

name: Walnut CBCT data collection (CWI FleX-ray)
aka: Cone-beam X-ray CT data collection designed for machine learning
size: 42 walnuts, each scanned on three orbits; about 6 GB per walnut, 48.4 GB for samples 1-8 and six Zenodo records in all
annotation_detail: raw projections, scan geometry, preprocessing and reconstruction scripts and reference reconstructions (14-bit flat panel)
how_to_get: Zenodo records 2686726, 2686970, 2687386, 2687634, 2687896, 2688111; code at github.com/cicwi/WalnutReconstructionCodes
paper: Der Sarkissian H et al. A cone-beam X-ray computed tomography data collection designed for machine learning. Sci Data 2019;6:215. doi:10.1038/s41597-019-0235-y
notes: Clean lab cone-beam geometry with no anatomy, relevant only for testing a projector or reconstruction code.

name: RabbitCT
aka: RabbitCT benchmark for high-speed C-arm CT
size: 1 clinical C-arm CT scan with 496 projections
annotation_detail: benchmark framework for FBP speed and reconstruction error
how_to_get: The FAU page refers to www.rabbitct.com, whose domain no longer resolves (2026-10-17); no mirror found
paper: Rohkohl C et al. Technical Note: RabbitCT - an open platform for benchmarking 3D cone-beam reconstruction algorithms. Med Phys 2009;36(9):3940-3944. doi:10.1118/1.3180956
notes: A real angiographic C-arm sweep that is no longer obtainable; recorded so it is not searched for again.
